compensating.why: hop 4 drops a plus sign that opens a segment
hop 1 drops a trailing slash of the expression

ownership_reason: Only the gold holds a segment's decoded name together with its conversion to an element index; hops 1-4 hold the whole expression (and the pointer that follows its last segment) and get back an immutable pointer whose following segments are built inside the gold's own recursion (the trigger's segment is the second one). A hop cannot pre-filter, because the same expression gives the full strings, the property names and the indices, all asserted by the trigger, and it cannot recover the index in one line, because the pointer is immutable and compile/valueOf re-enter the chain. The added public constructor stores the index it is given (-1 if the segment matches no element) and, by its javadoc, does not inspect the segment. Mapping every negative index to -1 (at that constructor or at getMatchingIndex) hides the trigger's value but not the overflow: "/4294967296" still matches element 0 and "/4294967297" element 1. The convention is pinned outside the gold: JsonPointer._parseIndex, beside the facade, gives a 10-digit name above Integer.MAX_VALUE the index -1 ('beware of super long indexes'); the JSON number reader ParserBase._parseNumericValue reads a 10-digit integer as an int only when it is at most Integer.MAX_VALUE ('Could still fit in int, need to check') and ParserBase.convertNumberToInt refuses a long outside the int range ('out of range of int'); TestNumericValues testLongRange, testIntRange and testNumbers pin that step and testSimplePath pins the rest of the index rule; all pass on the variant.
